messages.subject: [CorpLing with R] How to keep track to the source file of each  concordance
parts:
Hi, all.

I've compiled a corpus of 100 files, and for now I'm concatenating all
files (dez.teses<-c(lp1,lp2,lp3,lp4,lp5,lp6,lp7,lp8,lp9,lp10, etc...)
before running my concordance script.
After doing that, though, I can't keep track of which of the files
each concordance came from, and this is something I need in my study.

I thought about running one script for each of the files, but I just
thought I'd ask for some help before doing something that seems to be
non-functional.

I apologize if my question is too silly or if it's explained somewhere
on the book. I'd really appreciate if you could me help out.

Looking forward to hearing back from you,
Fernanda

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] How to keep track to the source file of each  concordance
parts:
Not silly at all!

### the long version you may put together given what's in the book:
# example data
lp1 <- c("ab", "cd", "ed")
lp2 <- c("gh", "ij", "kl")
lp3 <- c("mn", "op", "qr")

# prep
all.in.one.list <- list(lp1, lp2, lp3) # this you would need to so
while you scan in the files
number.of.files <- length(all.in.one.list)
all.lps <- character() # create an empty vector for what will be the
complete file

for (i in seq(number.of.files)) {
all.lps <- append(all.lps, paste("File_", i, "\t",
all.in.one.list[[i]], sep=""))
}

all.lps # the number before the tab says which file the 'sentence' is from



### the shorter version ;-)
as.character(mapply(paste, paste("File_", 1:length(all.in.one.list),
sep=""), all.in.one.list, sep="\t"))

Cheers,
STG

messages.author: 3edc58ee737edd94
messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Re: How to keep track to the source file of  each concordance
parts: Same problem as before:
> as.character(mapply(paste, paste("File_", 1:length(all.in.one.list), sep=""), all.in.one.list, sep="\t"))-> lings_file

this line inserts a tab stop and a tab but ...

> lings_file2<-unlist(strsplit(lings_file,"\\W+"))
... this line uses non-word characters (i.e., also tab stops) to split
up stuff, hence the tabs are gone.

Without (made-up) example data, it's more difficult to give advice but
it seems like you want to cat the file name first:

{ cat(FILENAME, "\t", lings_file3[max(0,i-10):max(0,i-1)], "\t",

lings_file3[i], "\t",
lings_file3[(i+1):min(i+10,length(lings_file3)+1)], "\n",
file=output.file, append=T) }

STG
